author: Stephen S Sarro
html: I was in a car accident when I was 4 years old. I received trauma to the head. I was in a coma for 16 days. I had to learn everything all over again. My cousin did not survive the accident. When we arrived at the hospital…the doctors informed my uncle (Mother was in too bad a shape for doctors to talk to) that he should get all family members to the hospital ASAP. The doctors told my family that my life was in God’s hands…there was nothing they could do for me. They gave me less than 10 hours to live. 50 years later…I’m still here. I do have short term memory loss and other issues to deal with but I am here.

author: kidinjurylaw
html: Mr. Sarro, I’m glad you’re still here and able to share your survival story! Thank you for sharing your story. It sounds like your injuries were obvious to everyone, at least during that initial period of coma, and you were treated quickly. I’ve had clients who suffered “mild” traumatic brain injuries and had a nightmare of a time getting anyone to recognize what has happened or treat them. Sometimes it’s a uninterested doctor, other times it is just that the imaging technology has not developed to the point where all brain injuries can be detected on scan (some axonal shearing is microscopic, for instance). Either way, when our master organ (the brain) is injured, we all need all the help we can find to get better. Thank you for commenting.

author: shandell milliman/broussard
html: My autistic son was injured in sept.2013 when 3 teachers supervised by the principal forced him on the bus.he had bruises showing finger prints along with a large scratch mark. The super.says the video’s don’t show the injuries so i don’t have a case. Already the school board is protecting them while a mother in the same situation would be charged automatically. I plan to fight this all the way to the capital. I will not give up! This is only showing teachers across America they can get away with this. How in the world is this acceptable?

author: kidinjurylaw
html:
It is not acceptable. The Georgia legislature and the Georgia Court of Appeals protect school officials from exposure to civil liability. It is, in my opinion, an abuse of power for one branch of the State to shield another branch from liability for negligent acts. The State makes education mandatory for our children and there should be a corresponding responsibility for safeguarding our children while they are at school.

And you are absolutely correct, if your son showed up at school with bruises and fingerprints, it is highly likely DFACS would receive a call from school officials and you would be investigated. So it’s a double standard.

I’m so sorry your son was hurt. If enough parents band together and vote for representatives and Judges that would address this injustice, change is possible.

Thank you for sharing your comment.

Attorney Pete Pearson

author: kidinjurylaw
html: Thank you for the link. This is yet another story illustrating the incestuous relationship between Courts and government school officials. We need the legislature to step in and instruct Courts to stop shielding dangerous teachers from civil liability. No accountability = no deterrence for future like conduct. The current state of the law in Georgia is unjust and reform is needed. Thank you again.

author: Eve
html:
I wanted to thank you for being so open and concise about child injury settlements in Ga.
I also thought you might want to know that the resources listed for this article are not found when i clicked the links. Do you know why that may be? I want to look more deeply into this important matter as we have reached settlement with the insurance company and after medicaid gets their requested portion back the settlement is just less than 15,000 fo my 10 year old.
Imagine my surprise when I found out from my lawyers that we now need to wait for a judge to look it over and sign off. On one hand I get it.. But on the other.. Its crazy. I wasnt at fault but they didnt catch the guy so its not millions of dollars. Just uninsured medical up to 25,000.
The car accident severely injured me and my child needs counseling to get over the trauma but was only minorly physically injured. We are lucky to have lived but I cant work now and if something doesnt happen financially soon to help us we are never going to recover no matter what. Altogether our medical bills total right a million. I am a single parent. Very very worried. Anyway.. Its not like anyone says hey theres a difference between a settlement for a kid and an adult. Thank you again for this info. I bookmarked your site. You rock.

html:
